pages.text: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ gives out heat (ΔH = −198 kJ/mol, ΔS = −188 J/mol·K): the cooler the bed, the further it goes - but vanadium only lights off near 670 K, and is faster hotter (Eₐ ≈ 90 kJ/mol). The gas is cooled between three beds so each runs where the equilibrium still allows a high conversion. More oxygen pushes it on, but dilutes the gas.
$(thing)Set$(): Bed temperature, Oxygen excess.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Bed temperature drift: the rate sees T·(1 ± 0.5%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): The vanadium beds are below light-off: they do nothing; The vanadium beds are over 600 °C: they sinter.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Sulfur trioxide made: the conversion, how fast the bed works, and how much the extra air dilutes the gas.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)ΔG°: ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS$(br)Equilibrium constant: K = e^(−ΔG°/RT)$(br)Equilibrium conversion: X/(1 − X) = √(K·p_O₂)$(br)Bed activity: k/k₇₂₃ = e^(−Eₐ/R·(1/T − 1/723 K))$(br)Conversion per pass: X = X_eq·(1 − e^(−3k))
